introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown: A dilute solution of sodium chloride is electrolysed using copper electrodes.

questions.enonce_markdown: State one common observation at the cathode and anode. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Cathode:** colourless bubbles of a gas (hydrogen) are given off.
- **Anode:** the copper anode **dissolves** (becomes thinner) and the solution around it turns blue.

(One observation at each electrode is enough.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write an equation for the reaction at each electrode.

Cathode: ...

Anode: ... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Cathode** (reduction): hydrogen ions from water are discharged in preference to sodium ions: $2\mathrm{H^+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2}$
- **Anode** (oxidation): the copper electrode is not inert, so the copper itself goes into solution: $\mathrm{Cu} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2e^-$

questions.enonce_markdown:
A steady current of 2A is passed through the electrolyte for 1 hour 16 minutes.

(i) Calculate the quantity of electricity in Coulombs. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Calculate the number of Faradays of electricity used. *[2 marks]*

(iii) What volume of the gas will be liberated at the cathode at r.t.p.? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Time: $t = 1\ \text{h}\ 16\ \text{min} = 3600 + 16\times60 = 4560$ s.

$Q = It = 2\times 4560 = \mathbf{9120\ C}$.

(ii) $1\ \text{faraday} = 96000$ C, so the number of faradays $= \dfrac{9120}{96000} = \mathbf{0.095\ F}$.

(iii) The gas at the cathode is hydrogen: $2\mathrm{H^+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2}$. So $2$ F liberate $1$ mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$, i.e. $24000\ \text{cm}^3$ at r.t.p., and $1$ F liberates $12000\ \text{cm}^3$.

Volume $= 0.095\times 12000 = \mathbf{1140\ cm^3}$ (1.14 dm$^3$).
